# The Big Fat Geek — Complete Archive & LLM Index

> Full archive of all articles, essays, and publications on The Big Fat Geek (https://kidakaka.com) by Prasad Ajinkya. Contains 94 articles published between 2008 and 2026.

## Core Information
- Site: https://kidakaka.com
- Author: Prasad Ajinkya (prasad@kidakaka.com)
- Focus: Agentic AI, Deterministic AI memory, Multi-agent orchestration, Enterprise software, Indian Fintech & Micro-lending, Engineering leadership, Data Analytics.

## 2013 (1 articles)

- **Date**: 6 January 2013
- **Categories**: Technology, Analytics
- **Summary**: The __utmz cookie is the Google Analytics traffic source cookie. - **Summary**: There are weeks that drain you completely. Not from any single dramatic event, but from the accumulated weight of small decisions, small disappointments, and the relentless forward motion that life demands even when you would rather stop.

### [Faith](https://kidakaka.com/2008/04/07/faith/)
- **Date**: 7 April 2008
- **Categories**: Thoughts, Life
- **Summary**: Faith is a word that gets used in two very different ways, and confusing them causes a lot of unnecessary argument. There is faith as a religious or spiritual concept, and there is faith as a practical operating principle — the willingness to act before you have proof.

### [D-Wars](https://kidakaka.com/2008/04/04/d-wars/)
- **Date**: 4 April 2008
- **Categories**: Movies
- **Summary**: D-Wars (Dragon Wars) is a South Korean monster film that made it to international screens on the strength of its visual effects budget and the universal appeal of giant creatures destroying city blocks. It is exactly what it looks like: an effects showcase with a story attached to justify the destruction.

### [5 Years Hence](https://kidakaka.com/2008/04/04/5-years-hence/)
- **Date**: 4 April 2008
- **Categories**: Thoughts, Life
- **Summary**: Five years is an interesting unit of time to think about. Short enough to feel concrete, long enough to allow for genuine transformation. Where will you be in five years? What will you have built, broken, learned, abandoned?

### [Nostalgia](https://kidakaka.com/2008/04/02/nostalgia/)
- **Date**: 2 April 2008
- **Categories**: Life, Thoughts
- **Summary**: Nostalgia is a peculiar emotion. It is not quite happiness and not quite sadness — it sits somewhere between them, a kind of sweet ache for things that no longer exist in the form you remember them.

### [Savalee — The Acorn and the Oak](https://kidakaka.com/2008/03/20/savalee-the-acorn-and-the-oak/)
- **Date**: 20 March 2008
- **Categories**: Thoughts, Life
- **Summary**: The Marathi word savalee means shadow — specifically the pleasant shade cast by a large tree. It carries connotations of shelter, rest, and the kind of cool refuge you seek on a hot afternoon. It is a word with comfort built into it.

### [Stardust](https://kidakaka.com/2008/03/18/stardust/)
- **Date**: 18 March 2008
- **Categories**: Movies
- **Summary**: Stardust is a fairy tale for adults — based on Neil Gaiman and Charles Vess’s illustrated novel — and it is one of the more delightful films to come out of the fantasy genre in years. It does not take itself too seriously, and that lightness is precisely what makes it work.

### [Bandwidth](https://kidakaka.com/2008/03/18/bandwidth/)
- **Date**: 18 March 2008
- **Categories**: Technology, Thoughts
- **Summary**: Bandwidth has become a metaphor as much as a technical term. We talk about personal bandwidth, cognitive bandwidth, emotional bandwidth — and by this we mean the same thing the engineers mean: the capacity to carry information, to process throughput, to handle simultaneous signals without degradation.

### [IE8 — We Are Not the Devil Anymore](https://kidakaka.com/2008/03/08/ie8-we-are-not-the-devil-anymore/)
- **Date**: 8 March 2008
- **Categories**: Technology
- **Summary**: Microsoft announced Internet Explorer 8 with a significant commitment: it would pass the Acid2 browser compatibility test in its default rendering mode. For web developers who had spent years cursing IE6 and its creative interpretations of CSS standards, this was news worth paying attention to.

### [Fire the Product Placement Guy](https://kidakaka.com/2008/02/07/fire-the-product-placement-guy/)
- **Date**: 7 February 2008
- **Categories**: Ads, Movies
- **Summary**: Product placement in films has a spectrum. At one end, it is seamless — the brand exists in the world of the film the way brands exist in the real world, noticed peripherally and unremarked upon. At the other end, it stops the film dead while a character explains the features of a car or the benefits of a soft drink to no one in particular. The latter is what I want to talk about.
